stem.en:
The long stone staircase that joins the harbour of Pollock Bay to the upper town used to be grey and a little gloomy. Last summer, thirty teenagers from the youth club spent four weekends painting each of its 140 steps a different colour. The paint was given by a local shop. Now visitors stop on the stairs to take photographs, and older residents say the climb feels shorter, even though it is just as steep.

What is the text mainly about?

options.en: How teenagers brightened an old town staircase
Why the climb from the harbour to the upper town is so steep
A shop near the harbour that sells paint
How many visitors come to Pollock Bay each summer

why.en: The text is about teenagers painting the grey staircase in bright colours. The shop is a detail; it never says why the climb is steep or how many people visit.
why.uz: Matn oʻsmirlar kulrang zinapoyani rang-barang boʻyagani haqida. Doʻkon — tafsilot; zina nega tikligi va mehmonlar soni aytilmagan.

We are asking families to give any board games, card games or jigsaw puzzles that they no longer use. Games should have all their pieces, as missing parts lead to arguments! The hillside above the village of Brenmoor was once covered in thorny bushes that nobody could cut back, because the slope was too steep for machines. Two years ago, the village tried something different: it borrowed a herd of forty goats from a farm nearby. The goats ate the bushes down in a single summer. Now wild flowers grow on the slope again, and families walk there on Sunday afternoons.

Which wild flowers now grow on the hillsides near Brenmoor

stem.en:
When Nodira's little brother started at Parkside School, he was the only pupil who could not hear. Nodira, who is fourteen, decided to start a lunchtime club to teach other pupils some sign language. At first only five friends came. Now more than sixty pupils go every week, and her brother can chat with children in his class without a teacher's help.

Nodira's brother is the only pupil at Parkside who can use sign language.

Teachers at Parkside School teach sign language in every lesson.

why.en: The club grew from five pupils to over sixty, and now her brother chats with his class. Five was only the start, and teachers do not run the club.

stem.en:
In the village of Sarbon, every family used to dry its apricots on the flat roof of its own house and sell them to whichever trader came by. Prices were low, and dust and birds spoiled much of the fruit. Five years ago, twenty families built a shared drying house with fine nets over the windows. They now dry their fruit together, sell it under one name and agree on a price before the traders arrive.

What is the text mainly about?

Why the birds of Sarbon like to eat the apricots on the roofs
How to build a flat roof that is good for drying fruit in summer
Why traders no longer come to the village of Sarbon

why.en: The text moves from each family working alone to twenty families drying and selling together. The birds are a detail, and traders still come.

stem.en:
Parents in the town of Wellby were worried about the traffic outside the primary school every morning. So they set up a walking bus: two adults walk a fixed route, and children join it at stops along the way, like passengers on a real bus. Within a term, the number of cars at the school gate fell, and teachers noticed that the children who walked arrived calmer and ready to learn.

What is the main idea of the text?

options.en: Walking to school together cut traffic and helped children start the day well.
Most parents in Wellby still drive their children to the school gate every day.
The walking bus uses a real bus for part of its route.
Teachers at the school asked parents to pay for a new school bus.

why.en: Worry about traffic, then the walking bus, then fewer cars and calmer children. It is only like a bus: no real bus is used or bought.
why.uz: Avval tirbandlikdan tashvish, keyin «piyoda avtobus», soʻng mashinalar kamayib, bolalar xotirjam keladigan boʻldi. Bu faqat avtobusga oʻxshaydi, haqiqiy avtobus yoʻq.

stem.en:
The Little Lantern puppet theatre has no building of its own. Its three puppeteers carry their stage, lights and forty puppets in an old van, and from spring to autumn they drive from one mountain village to the next. They perform in school halls, barns and, on fine evenings, in village squares. Many of the children who watch them have never been to a theatre in a town, which is exactly why the group started.

What is the text mainly about?

How the puppeteers make forty puppets by hand

A theatre building in town that children visit in spring

stem.en:
When the council of Harlow Moss proposed dimming the street lights after midnight, many residents objected, fearing that the darker streets would invite crime. The council agreed to a one-year trial and promised to brighten the lights again at once if problems appeared. In the event, the police recorded no change in crime, the council's electricity bill dropped noticeably, and an unexpected benefit emerged: for the first time in decades, residents could see the stars from their own gardens.

Which sentence best sums up the text?

options.en: A feared trial of dimmer night lights saved money and did not raise crime.
Residents of Harlow Moss asked the council to dim the street lights at night.
The darker streets led to more crime, so the lights were made bright again.
Harlow Moss has become a popular place for visitors who come to watch the stars.

why.en: Fears first, then a trial, then no change in crime and a lower bill. Residents objected rather than asked, and star-watching visitors are never mentioned.
why.uz: Avval qoʻrquv, keyin sinov, soʻng natija: jinoyatlar soni oʻzgarmadi, elektr uchun toʻlov kamaydi. Aholi buni soʻramagan, qarshi chiqqan; yulduz tomosha qiluvchi mehmonlar tilga olinmagan.
why.ru: Сначала страхи, затем пробный год, потом преступность не изменилась, а счёт за электричество снизился. Жители возражали, а не просили; о туристах, которые приезжают смотреть на звёзды, не сказано.

stem.en:
At Tenbury College, most students had switched to typing their lecture notes, and the teachers assumed this was simply progress. Then a lecturer, curious, asked one group to take notes by hand for a term. They wrote far less, but because they could not copy every word, they had to decide what mattered. At the end of the term, that group explained the lectures more clearly than the typists, although both groups had attended the same talks.

What is the main idea of the text?

options.en: Writing notes by hand made one group think about what was important.
Students at Tenbury College type faster than they can write by hand.
The lecturer told every student to stop using computers in class.
Students who typed their notes went to more lectures than the others.

why.en: Writing by hand forced the group to choose what mattered, and they explained the lectures better. Only one group changed, and both went to the same talks.
why.uz: Qoʻlda yozish guruhni muhim narsani tanlashga majbur qildi va ular maʼruzalarni yaxshiroq tushuntirdi. Faqat bitta guruh qoʻlda yozdi; ikkalasi bir xil maʼruzalarga borgan.
why.ru: Письмо от руки заставило группу выбирать главное, и она лучше объясняла содержание лекций. Изменилась лишь одна группа; обе слушали одни и те же лекции.

stem.en:
The fountain in the square at Calloway had been dry for as long as anyone could remember, and most people assumed it had simply been switched off to save money. When engineers finally opened the pipes, they found the real cause: tree roots had grown through them. Replacing the old pipes would have been costly, so the town laid a new pipe beside them. The fountain now runs from May to September, and its stone basin has become a popular meeting point.

What is the text mainly about?

options.en: How a dry fountain's real problem was found and fixed
Why the town of Calloway switched off its fountain to save money
How tree roots can damage the pipes under old buildings
A meeting point in Calloway that is busy all year round

why.en: People blamed saving money, but roots were the cause, and a new pipe got the fountain running. Roots are a detail here, and it runs only from May to September.
why.uz: Odamlar pul tejashni sabab deb oʻylagan, aslida ildizlar aybdor edi, yangi quvur favvorani qayta ishga tushirdi. Ildizlar — tafsilot; favvora faqat maydan sentyabrgacha ishlaydi.

stem.en:
The cable car from the village of Alpin Ford to the top of Mount Serra runs every twenty minutes from nine in the morning. The ride up takes eight minutes and climbs almost a thousand metres. At the top there is a small café and a viewing platform. In strong winds the cable car stops, and a sign at the bottom station tells visitors when it will open again.

How long does the ride to the top take?

options.en: eight minutes
twenty minutes
a thousand metres
nine o'clock

why.en: “eight minutes”: “The ride up takes eight minutes”. Twenty minutes is how often it runs, and the thousand metres is how high it climbs.
why.uz: «eight minutes»: «The ride up takes eight minutes». Yigirma daqiqa — qatnov oraligʻi; ming metr — koʻtarilish balandligi.
why.ru: «eight minutes»: «The ride up takes eight minutes». Двадцать минут — интервал между рейсами, тысяча метров — высота подъёма.

stem.en:
Volunteers at the Ellery river clean-up last weekend worked in teams of six along a five-kilometre stretch of the bank. In total, forty-two people took part, eight more than the year before. Between them they filled ninety bags with rubbish, and they pulled out three shopping trolleys and an old bicycle. The organisers hope that even more people will come next year.

forty-two

why.en: “thirty-four”: forty-two took part, “eight more than the year before”, so 42 − 8 = 34. Fifty adds the eight instead; eight is only the difference.
why.uz: «thirty-four»: qirq ikki kishi qatnashgan, «eight more than the year before», demak 42 − 8 = 34. Ellik — sakkiz ayirilmay, qoʻshilsa chiqadigan son; sakkiz — farq.

stem.en:
Before the tunnel under Corby Hill opened, drivers from Marsh End to the coast had to follow a winding road over the top, a journey of about fifty minutes in good weather. The new tunnel is two kilometres long, and the same trip now takes twenty minutes. Lorries over four metres high still have to use the old road, and the tunnel closes one night a month for cleaning.

How much time does the tunnel save on the trip from Marsh End to the coast?

twenty minutes
about fifty minutes
one night a month

why.en: “about thirty minutes”: the old road took about fifty, the tunnel trip takes twenty, so it saves about thirty. Twenty and fifty are the two journey times.

The Kingsmere sports centre lets members bring a guest. On weekdays before 5 p.m., a guest pays three pounds; after 5 p.m. and at weekends, the price is five pounds. The Moorside walking group was started fifteen years ago by four neighbours who wanted to keep fit. At first they walked together every evening. As more people joined, evening walks became hard to organise, and the group switched to two walks a week, on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Since last spring, a second, faster group has also gone out every Thursday, while the original group has kept to its old days.

Most visitors to the Fennamoor fish hatchery come to see the young trout swimming in long tanks. But the hatchery is also a working business: each spring it releases thousands of young fish into the rivers of the region, where they grow and are later caught by anglers. The money from fishing permits pays for the work, and the hatchery also sells fish to farms.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: More than a place to watch fish
How to get a fishing permit
Why trout grow so quickly in tanks
A family day out at a fish farm

why.en: “More than a place to watch fish”: visitors see the trout, but it is also a business that stocks the rivers. Permits pay for it but are not explained.
why.uz: «More than a place to watch fish»: mehmonlar baliq koʻradi, lekin bu daryolarga baliq qoʻyib yuboradigan korxona ham. Ruxsatnoma olish tushuntirilmagan.
why.ru: «More than a place to watch fish»: гости смотрят на форель, но это ещё и предприятие, которое зарыбляет реки. Как получить разрешение, не объясняется.

stem.en:
The Monday choir at Fallowfield Hall has one rule: nobody has to read music, and nobody is turned away for singing badly. Most of its forty members joined because they had been told as children that they could not sing. The choir leader teaches every song by ear, one line at a time. Last month the choir gave its first concert, and every seat in the hall was taken.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A choir that welcomes every voice
Learning to read music in a month
Why children stop singing at school
The hall's busiest night of the year

why.en: “A choir that welcomes every voice”: no music reading, and no one is turned away. Reading music is not taught, and the full hall is one detail.
why.uz: «A choir that welcomes every voice»: nota bilish shart emas, hech kim qaytarilmaydi. Nota oʻrgatilmaydi; toʻla zal — bitta tafsilot.
why.ru: «A choir that welcomes every voice»: ноты знать не нужно, никого не прогоняют. Нотам не учат; полный зал — лишь деталь.

stem.en:
A  The road between Elsby and Morrow runs along the foot of the cliffs. For many years it was the only way to drive from one village to the other.

B  After a rockfall blocked the road for a whole winter, the two villages agreed to build a new road inland. It took three years to finish, but it is safer, and the old cliff road is now open only to walkers and cyclists.

Choose the best heading for paragraph B.

options.en: A rockfall leads to a safer road
A road at the foot of the cliffs
Cycling holidays on the coast
How fallen rocks are cleared

why.en: “A rockfall leads to a safer road”: B goes from the blocked road to the new one inland. The road below the cliffs is A; clearing rocks is not described.
why.uz: «A rockfall leads to a safer road»: B da toʻsilib qolgan yoʻl oʻrniga ichkariroqdan yangi yoʻl qurilgani aytiladi. Qoya ostidagi yoʻl — A haqida; toshlarni tozalash tasvirlanmagan.
why.ru: «A rockfall leads to a safer road»: в B дорогу перекрыл обвал, и построили новую, подальше от берега. Дорога под скалами — это A; расчистку камней не описывают.

stem.en:
When the bus company in Tolland replaced its ticket offices with machines, the six people who had sold tickets did not lose their jobs. They now travel on the buses at busy times, helping older passengers and answering questions about routes. The company says complaints have fallen, and passengers often say they prefer a real person on the bus to a phone number.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: New work for the old ticket sellers
How to buy a ticket from a machine
Passengers complain about the machines
The busiest bus routes in Tolland

why.en: “New work for the old ticket sellers”: machines replaced the offices, and the sellers now help on the buses. Complaints fell, not rose; routes are not listed.
why.uz: «New work for the old ticket sellers»: kassalar oʻrnini avtomatlar egalladi, sotuvchilar endi avtobusda yordam beradi. Shikoyatlar kamaygan; yoʻnalishlar sanalmagan.
why.ru: «New work for the old ticket sellers»: автоматы заменили кассы, а кассиры теперь помогают в автобусах. Жалоб стало меньше; маршруты не перечислены.

stem.en:
The Okoro family started making candles as a hobby in their kitchen. Friends asked for candles of their own, then friends of friends, and soon the family was working every weekend to keep up. Three years ago they rented a small workshop, and today they sell their candles to shops in four countries, though every candle is still finished by hand.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: From a hobby to a growing business
How to make candles safely at home
Why the family had to leave their house
Machines that make candles quickly

why.en: “From a hobby to a growing business”: a kitchen hobby became a workshop selling abroad. Candles are still finished by hand, and no move from the house is mentioned.
why.uz: «From a hobby to a growing business»: oshxonadagi qiziqish chet elga sotadigan ustaxonaga aylandi. Shamlar hali ham qoʻlda tugatiladi; uydan koʻchish aytilmagan.
why.ru: «From a hobby to a growing business»: хобби на кухне стало мастерской с продажами за рубеж. Свечи по-прежнему доделывают вручную; о переезде ни слова.

stem.en:
Few people outside the valley had heard of the waterfall at Rendle Gill until a walker posted a photograph of it online. Within weeks, hundreds of visitors were coming every weekend, and the narrow lane to the falls was blocked with parked cars. The farmer who owns the land has now opened a field at the bottom as a car park and asks visitors to walk the last kilometre.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A photo brings crowds to a quiet place
The highest waterfall in the country
How to take good photographs of falling water
A farmer closes the lane to visitors

why.en: “A photo brings crowds to a quiet place”: one photo online, then crowds and a blocked lane. The farmer opened a car park; he did not close the lane.
why.uz: «A photo brings crowds to a quiet place»: bitta surat, keyin olomon va toʻsilgan yoʻl. Fermer avtoturargoh ochgan, yoʻlni yopmagan.
why.ru: «A photo brings crowds to a quiet place»: одно фото в сети, затем толпы и забитая дорога. Фермер открыл стоянку, а не закрыл дорогу.

stem.en:
In Larrow, as in many towns, people with gardens often have more apples or plums than they can eat, while others cannot afford fresh fruit. A group called Fruit Share now keeps a list of trees whose owners are happy for the fruit to be picked. Each autumn, volunteers pick it, give a share to the owner and take the rest to schools and a food bank. Nothing is sold.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Spare garden fruit finds a use
Growing apples in a small garden
Selling garden fruit at the market
Why fresh fruit costs so much

why.en: “Spare garden fruit finds a use”: fruit that would go to waste is picked and given away. Nothing is sold, and why fruit is dear is not explained.
why.uz: «Spare garden fruit finds a use»: isrof boʻladigan meva terilib, tarqatiladi. Hech narsa sotilmaydi; meva nega qimmatligi tushuntirilmagan.
why.ru: «Spare garden fruit finds a use»: фрукты, которые пропали бы, собирают и раздают. Ничего не продают; почему фрукты дороги, не объясняется.

stem.en:
When online shopping took most of the customers from the toy shop on Bell Street, its owner thought about closing. Instead she turned the back room into a place where children can play with the toys before their parents buy them, and on Saturdays she runs a board-game club. Families now travel from other towns to visit, and sales are higher than they were five years ago.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Play saves a struggling toy shop
Why online shopping is cheaper
A board-game club for parents
A toy shop closes after many years

why.en: “Play saves a struggling toy shop”: losing customers, the owner let children play, and sales rose. The club is a detail; the shop did not close.
why.uz: «Play saves a struggling toy shop»: xaridor kamaygach, egasi bolalarga oʻynashga ruxsat berdi, savdo oshdi. Klub — tafsilot; doʻkon yopilmagan.
why.ru: «Play saves a struggling toy shop»: теряя покупателей, хозяйка разрешила детям играть с игрушками, и продажи выросли. Клуб — деталь; магазин не закрылся.

stem.en:
Most houses in the hill village of Oberra cannot be reached by car, because the streets are steep flights of steps rather than roads. For centuries, goods were carried up on the backs of donkeys. Today the village still keeps six donkeys, which carry shopping, building materials and even furniture from the car park at the bottom to the houses at the top.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Donkeys still do the carrying
A new road is built for the village
Why the streets of Oberra are so steep
Buying a donkey at the market

why.en: “Donkeys still do the carrying”: with steps for streets, donkeys carry goods today as in the past. No road is built, and why the streets are steep is not said.
why.uz: «Donkeys still do the carrying»: koʻchalar zinapoya, shuning uchun yuklarni hamon eshaklar tashiydi. Yoʻl qurilmagan; koʻchalar nega tikligi aytilmagan.
why.ru: «Donkeys still do the carrying»: улицы — это лестницы, и грузы по-прежнему возят ослы. Дорогу не строят; почему улицы крутые, не сказано.

stem.en:
Belverton's council used to repaint the lines on its roads every spring, whether they needed it or not. Three years ago, it began asking cyclists and bus drivers to report faded lines through a phone app instead. Some drivers grumbled at first that the app was hard to use. The work is now done only where it is needed, and the money saved has paid for twenty new pedestrian crossings near schools.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Smart repainting pays for crossings
A yearly repaint that never changes
How to download the council's app
Cyclists complain about faded lines

why.en: “Smart repainting pays for crossings”: reports send the painting where it is needed, and the savings buy crossings. The app is a detail; the yearly repaint has stopped.
why.uz: «Smart repainting pays for crossings»: xabarlar boʻyashni kerakli joyga yoʻnaltiradi, tejalgan pul oʻtish joylariga ketadi. Ilova — tafsilot; har yilgi boʻyash toʻxtagan.
why.ru: «Smart repainting pays for crossings»: по сообщениям красят только там, где нужно, а сэкономленные деньги идут на переходы. Приложение — деталь; ежегодной покраски больше нет.

stem.en:
It is often assumed that the steep terraces on the hillsides around Lusa were cut to grow grapes. Old letters kept in the village tell a different story: the terraces were first built for mulberry trees, whose leaves fed silkworms. Only when the silk trade failed did farmers turn to grapes, and few visitors today realise that the vineyards stand on ground shaped for a very different crop.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: What the terraces were first for
How grapes are grown on steep hills
The village's famous silk market
Visitors who come to Lusa for the wine

why.en: “What the terraces were first for”: they were built for mulberries, not grapes, as few now know. Growing grapes and visitors are not the point; no market is named.
why.uz: «What the terraces were first for»: zinapoyali dalalar uzum emas, tut uchun qurilgan — buni kam odam biladi. Uzum va mehmonlar asosiy emas; bozor tilga olinmagan.
why.ru: «What the terraces were first for»: террасы строили для шелковицы, а не для винограда, и мало кто это знает. Виноградарство и гости не главное; рынок не упоминается.

stem.en:
A  The Tarrin Valley railway was built to carry wool from the hill farms to the mills in the city. For seventy years it ran four trains a day, and almost every family in the valley depended on it.

B  When the mills closed, the line lost its main trade, and passengers alone could not keep it going. The last train ran on a winter morning. Within ten years, half of the families had moved away, and several of the valley's schools had shut.

Choose the best heading for paragraph B.

options.en: A closure that emptied the valley
A railway built for the wool trade
Plans to reopen the old line
Why the mills moved to the city

why.en: “A closure that emptied the valley”: B tells how the line closed and families and schools went. The wool trade is A; no plans to reopen are mentioned.
why.uz: «A closure that emptied the valley»: B temir yoʻl yopilib, oilalar ketgani va maktablar yopilganini aytadi. Jun savdosi — A; qayta ochish rejasi aytilmagan.
why.ru: «A closure that emptied the valley»: B о том, как закрыли линию и опустела долина. Шерсть — это A; о планах вновь открыть линию ни слова.

stem.en:
The beach at Port Selwyn was losing sand every winter, and the council's first idea was to bring in more by lorry. A retired fisherman pointed out that the trouble had started when a wall was built at the harbour mouth, changing the way the water moved along the shore. Engineers tested his idea, the wall was shortened, and within two winters the sand began to return on its own.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: An old fisherman finds the real cause
Lorries of sand save the beach at Port Selwyn
Why fishermen dislike harbour walls
A new wall is built at the harbour

why.en: “An old fisherman finds the real cause”: he linked the lost sand to the wall, and shortening it worked. Lorries were only a first idea, and no new wall is built.
why.uz: «An old fisherman finds the real cause»: u qum yoʻqolishini devor bilan bogʻladi, devor qisqartirilgach qum qaytdi. Yuk mashinalari — dastlabki fikr; yangi devor yoʻq.
why.ru: «An old fisherman finds the real cause»: он связал потерю песка со стеной, и когда стену укоротили, это помогло. Грузовики — лишь первая идея; новую стену не строят.

stem.en:
Farmers in the far north of the Tessel hills once had to drive their sick animals for half a day to reach a vet. Now a vet comes to them: a clinic in a converted lorry visits each village once a fortnight, with a table, medicines and even a small X-ray machine on board. Farmers book a visit by phone, and emergency calls are still answered from the town.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A clinic on wheels for farm animals
How to care for a sick animal
A new animal hospital opens in town
Why farmers are leaving the hills

why.en: “A clinic on wheels for farm animals”: instead of long drives, a clinic in a lorry visits the villages. No hospital opens, and farmers leaving is never mentioned.
why.uz: «A clinic on wheels for farm animals»: uzoq yoʻl oʻrniga yuk mashinasidagi klinika qishloqlarga keladi. Shifoxona ochilmagan; fermerlar ketishi aytilmagan.
why.ru: «A clinic on wheels for farm animals»: вместо долгой дороги клиника в грузовике приезжает в сёла. Больница не открывается; об отъезде фермеров ни слова.

stem.en:
A  For most of the last century, the river island at Wenmouth was used to graze cattle in summer. Every June the herd was walked across a shallow ford at low water, and every October it was walked back.

B  When the cattle were taken away for good, the island was left to itself. Within a decade it was thick with young willows and full of nesting birds, and it is now one of the few places on the river where otters are seen.

Choose the best heading for paragraph A.

options.en: A seasonal crossing for cattle
From farmland to a wild island
Where to see otters on the river
Why the cattle were taken away

why.en: “A seasonal crossing for cattle”: A tells how the herd was walked over each June and back each October. The wild island and the otters belong to B.
why.uz: «A seasonal crossing for cattle»: A podani har iyunda orolga oʻtkazib, oktabrda qaytarishni tasvirlaydi. Yovvoyi orol va undagi hayvonlar — B haqida.
why.ru: «A seasonal crossing for cattle»: A о том, как стадо каждый июнь переводили на остров и в октябре обратно. Дикий остров и выдры — это B.
